report.summary: Chunk 1 of 2 of grounding.py: defines ReferenceAudit, audit_references, claim_text, defined_in, imported_in, judge, module_names, and supporting regexes. Contains module-level docstring and comments with several checkable claims.
risks: audit_references | medium | The audit skips citations whose first path component is not in anchors; if anchors is empty (e.g., tracked paths have no subdirectories), all citations are silently ignored. | Add a fallback: if anchors is empty, treat every citation as a claim about the repository or skip nothing.
defined_in | low | Regex _ASSIGN_RE may match comments or strings containing `name =` patterns, leading to false positives. | Test against edge cases like strings or comments.
imported_in | low | Regex may misparse complex imports (e.g., parenthesized multi-line imports) and miss names. | Use AST-based parsing for reliability.
module_names | low | AST-based but catches only top-level name stores; nested assignments inside functions are ignored per spec. Not a bug but a design choice.
audit_references | low | Symbol resolution uses module_names which may miss names defined via `__all__` or dynamic assignment. | Consider adding `__all__` expansion.

handoff.purpose: Define data structures and functions for auditing references and judging existence claims in model output.

symbols.name: _DEF_RE
symbols.note: Regex to find def/class names at module level.

symbols.name: _REFERENCE
symbols.note: Regex to find file path and optional :symbol citations.

symbols.name: _ABSENCE
symbols.note: Regex to detect phrases asserting a name is absent.

symbols.name: _SELF_SCOPED
symbols.note: Regex to detect self-scoped absence claims.

symbols.name: _NAME
symbols.note: Regex to extract name candidates from text.

symbols.name: defined_in
symbols.note: Returns frozenset of names defined at module level via def, class, or assignment.

symbols.name: imported_in
symbols.note: Returns frozenset of names imported in the source.

symbols.name: module_names
symbols.note: Returns frozenset of all def/class names at any depth plus module-level bindings and imports using AST.

claims.text: Does what a model ASSERTED correspond to what is actually in the tree?
claims.why: The module defines audit_references and judge (to be defined) which answer that question.

claims.text: a model cites ``daedalus/spine/attempt.py:run_attempt`` -- is that file there, is that symbol in it? (:func:`audit_references`)
claims.why: audit_references resolves file paths and symbols; the example matches its purpose.

claims.text: a model says "X is never defined" -- can that be refuted mechanically? (:func:`judge`)
claims.why: judge is not defined in this chunk; will appear later.

claims.text: They are the same question about the same repository and they share the same index, so they live together.
claims.why: Both audit_references and judge (to be defined) operate on the same repository and file list.

claims.text: They were briefly implemented twice -- once in ``lanes/checks.py`` for reports and once in ``tools/funnel_report.py`` for funnel output -- and the two agreed numerically
claims.why: No code from those files is present; cannot verify historical duplication.

claims.text: This module is the merge.
claims.why: The module consolidates reference auditing and existence judging.

claims.text: ``checks.py`` asks whether a file a lane is about to WRITE is intact -- it runs before bytes hit the disk and returns a refusal. This asks whether a model's PROSE corresponds to the tree, and it returns a measurement.
claims.why: audit_references returns a ReferenceAudit measurement; judge (to be defined) returns a verdict. No refusal mechanism is present.

claims.text: A GRAMMAR check. It answers "does this name exist", never "is this claim true".
claims.why: defined_in, imported_in, module_names, audit_references, and judge (to be defined) all check existence, not truth.

claims.text: MEASURED 2026-07-30: a finding whose every reference resolved, which survived an adversarial review tier and ranked first in the resulting plan, was false -- `derive_task_from_commit` does populate the fields it was accused of ignoring, at `correctness.py:1444`. Nothing here would have caught that.
claims.why: The module only checks existence; semantic truth is explicitly out of scope.

claims.text: It is also, deliberately, an OBSERVATION rather than a refusal.
claims.why: audit_references returns a data object; no refusal mechanism.

claims.text: A report may legitimately name a runtime path or a file in another repository, and a fence that refused those would be wrong far more often than right.
claims.why: audit_references skips citations not anchored in the repository's own top-level directories, avoiding false positives for external paths.

claims.text: Names this file DEFINES: def, class, module-level assignment.
claims.why: defined_in uses _DEF_RE and _ASSIGN_RE to find def, class, and module-level assignments.

claims.text: Kept apart from :func:`defined_in` on purpose. A finding saying "X is not defined here" about a name the file imports is loose rather than false, and a metric whose whole job is proving things false must not spend its credibility on that distinction being blurred.
claims.why: imported_in returns only imported names; defined_in returns only defined names; they are separate functions.

claims.text: Every def/class at ANY depth, plus module-level bindings and imports.
claims.why: module_names uses ast.walk to find def/class at any depth, plus module-level Name stores and aliases.

claims.text: Unlike ``checks.toplevel_defs``, this descends: a citation naming ``events.py:TransportRecord.from_dict`` is naming a method, and a top-level-only reading would report every method in the repository absent.
claims.why: module_names walks the AST to any depth, so it finds methods and nested classes.

claims.text: What a report's file/symbol citations resolve to.
claims.why: ReferenceAudit stores counts and lists of resolved, repaired, ambiguous, invented, and absent symbols.

claims.text: MEASURED 2026-07-30 over a four-tier advisory funnel: of 42 unresolvable paths in its planning tier, 19 were a real file with its directory dropped, 1 shared a basename with another file, and 22 named a file that exists nowhere. Those need opposite responses -- repair, refuse to guess, discard -- and one number for all three is worth little.
claims.why: ReferenceAudit has separate fields for repaired, ambiguous, invented, and absent_symbols, providing granular data.

claims.text: ``tracked`` is the authoritative file list -- pass ``git ls-files`` output, never a filesystem walk, so ignored artefacts and a contributor's scratch files cannot make an invented path look real.
claims.why: audit_references takes tracked as a parameter and uses it as the authoritative set of paths.

claims.text: The repository's own top-level directories, derived from the file list rather than hardcoded. A cited path is an ASSERTION ABOUT THIS REPOSITORY only when it starts inside one of them.
claims.why: anchors is built from the first component of each tracked path; citations are skipped if their first component is not in anchors.

claims.text: Without this anchor the audit reported the docstring example ``a/b.py``, the runtime path ``RUN_DIR/last_report.json`` and the written type ``Any/typing.Any`` as invented files -- all measured, all noise.
claims.why: The anchor filtering prevents such false positives.

claims.text: Phrasings that assert a name is absent. Deliberately narrow: this judges only claims it can decide, and a wider net would score claims about BEHAVIOUR as if they were claims about EXISTENCE.
claims.why: _ABSENCE regex is defined with limited phrases; no regex for behavioural claims.

claims.text: `do|does` and not just `does`: a gold set caught "_body_sha and _entry_sha, which do not exist" scoring undecided while the singular scored false. A judge that sees one grammatical number has a blind spot nobody would think to look for.
claims.why: _ABSENCE includes both 'does' and 'do' in the pattern.

claims.text: A statement that scopes its own absence claim to the window it was shown.
claims.why: _SELF_SCOPED regex is defined to catch self-limiting phrases.

claims.text: MEASURED: the first version of this judge marked "AgentCapabilities and AgentEvent are not defined in this chunk" as provably false, because the names are imported by the file. That finding is TRUE and honest -- it names the scope it was given, and several such findings go on to say "expected to be defined elsewhere". Scoring a correct self-limited observation as a lie is the same cry-wolf failure this metric exists to count: 461 of them in one run, before this rule.
claims.why: _SELF_SCOPED regex is defined to detect such self-scoped claims, preventing false negatives.

observations.what: audit_references uses PurePosixPath to parse paths; on Windows, backslashes may not be handled correctly.
The anchor filtering may skip legitimate citations if the first path component is not a top-level directory (e.g., if the repo root is not in the path).
defined_in and imported_in use regex that may fail on edge cases like multiline strings or nested parentheses.
The module defines __all__ including claim_text and judge, but they are not present in this chunk; they will be defined later.
